boundary.title: Connect server to server
boundary.internal: API-key integration routes are private on backend:3002. They are not exposed through the browser gateway at http://localhost:3000 or the public TLS listener on port 3001.
boundary.protocol: The complete Travel Rule surface is mounted only when PROTOCOL=TRP is exact. Use the public listener only for identity, health, and authenticated TRP peer traffic.
boundary.secret: Issue a scoped X-API-Key to the calling service, keep it in server-side secret management, and never send it to browser code, logs, screenshots, or client storage.

apiDocs.quickstartDescription: Start with the protocol-neutral API for policy-driven orchestration, or use the direct TRP compatibility flow when your application already owns the TRP lifecycle.

steps.configureDescription: Use an API client credential with transfers:read and transfers:write. Add webhooks:manage before creating subscriptions. The one-time credential belongs in server-side secret management.
steps.preflightDescription: Run preflight before collecting or sending party data. The native_trp connector is currently the only runtime-supported connector, and every required capability must match.
steps.transferDescription: Send an 8–128 character Idempotency-Key and a strict policy input. Replace the Travel Address and valuation timestamp with current synthetic or production-approved values; the example intentionally contains no real PII.
steps.stateDescription: Treat transfer, case, and exchange states independently. Complete required information with expected_version, settle only a ready transfer, and handle 409 responses by reloading the latest state before retrying a decision.
steps.webhookDescription: Subscribe before production traffic. Verify X-Defy-Signature with the exact raw body, compare in constant time, reject stale timestamps, deduplicate X-Defy-Delivery, and acknowledge only after durable acceptance.

steps.configureDescription: Each VASP uses its own private backend:3002 API credential. Peer protocol delivery uses the Travel Address public origin, TLS 1.3, and certificates trusted by the receiving VASP.
steps.addressDescription: The receiving VASP creates a short-lived bearer Travel Address and returns it only to the trusted transfer workflow. Do not log, screenshot, or persist the bearer URL outside its intended lifecycle.
steps.transferDescription: The sending VASP submits the Travel Address, positive lowest-denomination amount, asset DTI, and valid IVMS 101.2020 or 101.2023 payload. A 202 response is durable and retryable, not a failed transfer.
steps.decisionDescription: An authorized reviewer uses the UI or JWT/OIDC inquiry API. Cookie mutations also require CSRF. A durable decision may return 202 when callback delivery needs a service-side retry.
steps.confirmationDescription: After approval, send exactly txid or canceled through the confirmation path. Retry only an eligible durable message; Defy records the protocol result and never broadcasts an on-chain transaction.

reference.description: Paths are case-sensitive and listener boundaries are part of the security contract. Cookie-authenticated mutations require the existing CSRF header in addition to the stated JWT/OIDC role.

endpointDescriptions.createV1Transfer: Create one client-isolated aggregate. Requires Idempotency-Key; an exact replay returns 200 and a changed payload returns 409.

endpointDescriptions.completeInformation: Merge approved mutable fields and re-evaluate policy using expected_version.
endpointDescriptions.cancelV1Transfer: Cancel locally and queue a remote cancellation only after counterparty progress or PII disclosure.
endpointDescriptions.settleV1Transfer: Move a ready transfer to released and queue settlement confirmation with a printable reference.
endpointDescriptions.preflight: Select the first healthy connector satisfying every required capability without sending party data.
endpointDescriptions.createWebhook: Create an HTTPS-only subscription with bounded event types and a 32–256 character signing secret.
endpointDescriptions.listWebhooks: List owned safe subscription metadata without returning URLs or signing secrets.
endpointDescriptions.disableWebhook: Disable one owned active webhook subscription.
endpointDescriptions.listCases: List the PII-free case queue with state, page, and limit filters.
endpointDescriptions.getCase: Return current case, transfer, exchange, approval, and optimistic-lock version.
endpointDescriptions.decideCase: Record an approved, rejected, or escalated decision with reason and expected_version.
endpointDescriptions.auditCase: Export related append-only events and the recomputed integrity result without decrypted party data.
endpointDescriptions.createReencryption: Start the single active resumable job for the configured active encryption key.
endpointDescriptions.listReencryption: List re-encryption job progress and terminal state.
endpointDescriptions.createTravelAddress: Create a short-lived beneficiary bearer Travel Address.
endpointDescriptions.createTrpTransfer: Create and deliver an outbound TRP transfer; 202 indicates durable retryable delivery.
endpointDescriptions.getTrpTransfer: Return transfer state and decrypted operation result without the IVMS payload.
endpointDescriptions.confirmTrpTransfer: Send exactly txid or canceled through the existing confirmation path.
endpointDescriptions.retryTrpTransfer: Retry the latest eligible durable message; returns 409 when no message qualifies.
endpointDescriptions.listInquiries: List reviewable inquiries with optional status and bounded pagination.
endpointDescriptions.getInquiry: Return the decrypted canonical IVMS 101.2023 inquiry detail for an authorized reviewer.
endpointDescriptions.decideInquiry: Record one approved or rejected decision and deliver the peer callback.
endpointDescriptions.analytics: Return bounded 7d, 30d, or 90d Travel Rule analytics with safe aggregate projections.
endpointDescriptions.listManagementResource: List the safe paginated projection for the selected management resource.
endpointDescriptions.getManagementResource: Return one safe resource detail; transfer and message details include server-derived actions.
endpointDescriptions.managementTravelAddress: Create a Travel Address through the administrator browser-safe mutation boundary.
endpointDescriptions.managementTransfer: Create an outbound TRP transfer through the administrator browser-safe mutation boundary.
endpointDescriptions.managementConfirm: Confirm or cancel an eligible outbound transfer through the management API.
endpointDescriptions.managementRetry: Retry the latest eligible management-visible protocol message.
endpointDescriptions.createEmailInvitation: Create an independent 30-day, single-use email invitation after the server-owned fallback delay.
endpointDescriptions.listEmailDeliveries: List safe recipient and delivery lifecycle metadata without tokens, digests, or provider responses.
endpointDescriptions.retryEmailDelivery: Requeue an eligible unexpired dead-lettered email while preserving its single-use token.
endpointDescriptions.consumeEmailAccess: Atomically consume a one-time fragment token and return only the structured read-only transfer summary.
endpointDescriptions.serviceStatus: Return the public service status object.
endpointDescriptions.liveness: Report whether the process is running without checking PostgreSQL.
endpointDescriptions.readiness: Check PostgreSQL readiness and return 503 while the dependency is unavailable.
endpointDescriptions.identity: Return the configured VASP name, LEI, and public certificate chain.
endpointDescriptions.protocolInquiry: Accept an authenticated TRP inquiry with api-version and request-identifier headers.
endpointDescriptions.protocolResolution: Accept an authenticated approved or rejected TRP resolution.
endpointDescriptions.protocolConfirmation: Accept an authenticated TRP transaction confirmation or cancellation.
